grades.reason: This is exactly the hole the merged change closes: `POST /authorize` (oauth.js:117) and `POST /bridge/authorize` (bridge.js:155) now run `requireLoginSession` before the handler, which refuses (and destroys) a revoked session with 401, writes no `Settings.mcpUserId` and issues no code — the cited line 103 is now the sign-in notice, not an identity write.

triageGrades.reason: The change adds an authentication guard (`requireLoginSession`) and session-revocation handling to both OAuth approval forms.
No secret storage, exposure or configuration changes; only fake test tokens are set in test env, which is not secrets handling.
Nothing billing-, quota- or AI-spend-related is touched.

The change adds no destructive data operation — the session `destroy()` is the pre-existing `refuseRevoked` path it reuses — and the cited evidence (oauth.test.js:78) is just a `process.env.CLIENT_ORIGIN` assignment.
No outbound calls or third-party integrations are added; the touched endpoints are inbound.
No version bump, dependency or deploy-config change — only server code, docs and tests.

summary: The local review produced no real findings: its single finding restates the vulnerability the merged diff fixes (so it is a false positive), and one triage answer ('destructive') is wrong with irrelevant evidence.
